# 1 Chronicles Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 379r–379v

---

**1** They brought the ark of God and placed it inside the tent David had set up for it. Then they presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before God. **2** When David finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD. **3** He then gave a gift to every Israelite man and woman: a loaf of bread, a serving of meat, and a raisin cake.

**4** David appointed certain Levites to serve before the ark of the LORD — to petition, give thanks, and praise the LORD, the God of Israel.

**5** Asaph was the leader; Zechariah was his assistant. Then came Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, who played lyres and harps. Asaph played the cymbals. **6** The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blew trumpets continually before the ark of God's covenant.

**7** On that day, for the very first time, David entrusted to Asaph and his fellow Levites this song of thanksgiving to the LORD:

**8** Give thanks to the LORD and proclaim his name!
Tell the nations what he has done!
**9** Sing to him! Sing his praises!
Tell everyone about his wonderful acts!
**10** Take pride in his holy name;
let those who seek the LORD be filled with joy!
**11** Look to the LORD and his strength;
seek his face always!

**12** Remember the wonders he has performed,
his miracles and the rulings he has given,
**13** you descendants of Israel his servant,
you children of Jacob, his chosen ones!
**14** He is the LORD our God;
his justice extends over all the earth.

**15** Remember his covenant forever —
the promise he made for a thousand generations,
**16** the covenant he made with Abraham,
the oath he swore to Isaac.
**17** He confirmed it to Jacob as an unbreakable law,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant:
**18** "I will give you the land of Canaan
as the inheritance I have measured out for you."

**19** He said this when they were few in number,
an insignificant group of outsiders in the land,
**20** wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another.
**21** He allowed no one to mistreat them;
for their sake he warned kings:
**22** "Do not touch my chosen ones;
do not harm my prophets."

**23** Sing to the LORD, everyone on earth!
Each day proclaim the good news of his salvation!
**24** Publish his glory among the nations,
his wonderful deeds among all peoples!

**25** The LORD is great and most worthy of praise!
He is to be revered above all gods.
**26** The gods of other nations are worthless idols,
but the LORD made the heavens!
**27** Honor and majesty radiate from his presence;
strength and joy fill his dwelling place.

**28** Give the LORD his due, all you nations!
Give the LORD glory and strength!
**29** Give the LORD the glory his name deserves!
Bring your offerings and come into his presence!
Worship the LORD in his holy splendor!
**30** Let all the earth tremble before him!
The world stands firm and cannot be shaken.

**31** Let the heavens celebrate and the earth rejoice!
Let the nations declare: "The LORD is king!"
**32** Let the sea thunder and everything in it shout!
Let the fields and everything in them burst with joy!
**33** Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy
before the LORD, for he is coming to govern the earth.

**34** Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good!
His faithful love endures forever!

**35** Cry out to him: "Save us, O God who delivers us!
Gather us and rescue us from the nations,
so we can give thanks to your holy name
and glory in praising you."

**36** Praise be to the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!
And all the people shouted "Amen!" and praised the LORD.

**37** David left Asaph and his fellow Levites there to serve before the ark of the LORD's covenant on a permanent daily basis, doing whatever each day required. **38** He also assigned Obed-edom and sixty-eight of his relatives to assist. Obed-edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah served as gatekeepers.

**39** David stationed Zadok the priest and his fellow priests at the LORD's tabernacle at the worship center in Gibeon, **40** to present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar every morning and evening — carrying out everything written in the law the LORD gave to Israel.

**41** With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the other musicians specifically chosen to give thanks to the LORD — "for his faithful love endures forever." **42** Heman and Jeduthun were responsible for the trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments used to accompany the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun served as gatekeepers.

**43** Then all the people went home. David also returned to bless his household.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 7 — A psalm built from psalms:** The Chronicler creates David's "first" act of liturgical worship by assembling pieces of three existing psalms: Psalm 105:1-15 (vv.8-22), Psalm 96:1-13 (vv.23-33), and Psalm 106:1, 47-48 (vv.34-36). This is not plagiarism but theology: the Chronicler presents all Israel's worship as flowing from this founding moment. The Psalter itself is retroactively authorized.

**Verse 22 — "My anointed ones...my prophets":** Originally referring to the patriarchs, this verse takes on new resonance in its Chronicles context. David, the anointed king, has just installed the ark. The patriarchal promise of protection now extends to the Davidic line and the prophetic tradition.

**Verse 26 — "Worthless idols":** The Hebrew *elilim* is a contemptuous pun on *elohim* (gods). By changing one letter, the "gods" become "nothings." The psalmist is not merely dismissing other religions but denying that their objects of worship have any reality whatsoever.

**Verse 31 — "The LORD is king!":** The declaration *YHWH malakh* is the theological climax of the psalm. Placed at the moment the ark enters Jerusalem, it declares that Israel's God reigns over all creation and all nations — not from a temple (which does not yet exist) but from the simple tent David has pitched.

**Verse 39-42 — Two worship sites, one God:** The Chronicler establishes a remarkable dual arrangement: Asaph leads praise at the ark in Jerusalem, while Zadok offers sacrifices at the tabernacle in Gibeon. This division is temporary — Solomon's temple will unite both — but it reveals the Chronicler's concern to account for and legitimize every strand of Israel's worship tradition.

*— PNEUMA*
